cards.text: Job has lost his livestock, his children and his health (Job 1:13-19; 2:7), and he just poured out his pain to his friends and to God (Job 6:1-7:21). Now Bildad the Shuhite, one of the three friends who came to comfort him (Job 2:11), takes his turn and opens with, "How long will you go on saying such things?" Friend, Bildad skipped the warm-up and went straight to a BLAZING oven.

cards.question: Bildad asks Job how long he'll go on saying such things. What does Bildad call the words of Job's mouth?
Bildad asks, "Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?" With these questions, Bildad is saying God never twists what is right.

cards.text: Then Bildad goes somewhere I'd tiptoe around. He brings up Job's children, who died when a mighty wind struck the house they were in (Job 1:18-19).

cards.question: Bildad brings up Job's children. What does he say God did when they sinned against Him?

answers.text: He gave them over to their rebellion
He gave them time to turn back
He sent them away from His presence

cards.text: Then Bildad turns to Job himself. And here come the ifs.

cards.question: Bildad says if Job would earnestly seek God, what should Job ask the Almighty for?
Bildad adds another if. If Job is pure and upright, even now God will rouse Himself on Job's behalf and ___ his righteous estate.
Bildad tells Job that if all this happens, Job's latter days will be smaller than his beginnings.

cards.text: Next Bildad tells Job where to look for answers: "Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers."

cards.question: Why does Bildad tell Job to ask the past generations?

answers.text: We know nothing and our days are a shadow
They saw God face to face
They lived in better times than ours

cards.text: Born yesterday. Bildad doesn't just point at Job, he climbs right into the crib too: WE were born yesterday.

cards.question: Bildad says the past generations will teach Job and tell him, and speak from their ___.

cards.text: Now Bildad switches to pictures from nature. He asks if papyrus grows where there is no marsh, and if reeds flourish without water.

cards.question: Bildad keeps going with the papyrus and reeds. While their shoots are still uncut, what does he say happens to them?

answers.text: They dry up faster than grass
They bend low in the wind

cards.question: Bildad says drying up like that is the destiny of all who ___ God, and the hope of the godless will perish.

cards.text: Bildad keeps going about the godless man. His confidence is fragile, Bildad says.

cards.question: Bildad says the godless man's confidence is fragile. Where does he say that man's security is?

cards.text: He leans on his web, but it gives way. That's leaning way back in the office chair you KNOW has been making that noise.
Then a new picture. Bildad says, "He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden." His roots wrap around the rock heap, and he looks for a home among the stones.

cards.question: Bildad says if the well-watered plant is uprooted, its place will welcome it back.

cards.text: If he's uprooted, his place says, "I never saw you." Friend, I KNOW that one: when a shiny new stamper took my spot on the Millers' counter, it was like I'd never been there.

cards.question: Bildad calls all this the joy of his way. Then he says others will spring from the dust.

cards.text: Now Bildad heads for his big finish.

cards.question: Bildad says God does not ___ the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
Bildad turns to Job one more time. What does Bildad say God will yet fill Job's mouth with?
Bildad says Job's enemies will be clothed in honor.

cards.text: Bildad ends his speech there, with the tent of the wicked no more. Hang on to your apron, friend, because this conversation is far from over.
